1.title: Weekly tip: How to use the subjunctive in Spanish
1.content: The subjunctive is one of the biggest challenges for Spanish learners. The key: use it after verbs of desire, emotion or doubt.
1.example: "Espero que llegues pronto" / "Quiero que seas feliz" — The main verb triggers the subjunctive.
1.author: Daisu Team

2.title: 7-day challenge: Speak only English · Streak x2
2.content: For 7 days, try to use only English in our chat rooms. Every message counts for your streak. The top 3 win an exclusive badge + double XP!
2.author: Daisu Community

3.title: Success story: María went from A2 to B1 in 3 months
3.content: "I came to Daisu barely able to speak. In 3 months of daily practice with natives, I passed my DELE B1 exam. It wouldn't have been possible without this community!"
3.author: María G.

4.title: New feature: Unlimited AI corrections in Pro plan
4.content: Pro users now have access to unlimited real-time automatic corrections. The system detects grammatical errors and suggests more natural alternatives.
4.author: Daisu Team

5.title: Vocabulary tournament: win badge + XP
5.content: Join our first vocabulary tournament. Each round, you get 10 words and must use them correctly in the chat. The winner gets the "Lexicon" badge.
5.author: Daisu Community

6.title: Duolingo launches AI conversational mode — what do you think?
6.content: Duolingo announced a mode where AI simulates real conversations. At Daisu we believe that more than AI, you need real humans. What do you prefer?
6.author: Editorial

7.title: How to understand the Brazilian accent quickly
7.content: Brazilian Portuguese has unique characteristics: syllable reduction, regional slang, and a different rhythm from European Portuguese. Practice by listening to podcasts and talking with Brazilians.
7.example: "Cê tá bem?" = "Você está bem?" — The reduction of "você" to "cê" is very common in informal Brazil.
7.author: Daisu Team

8.title: New study: speaking 15 min a day accelerates learning 3x
8.content: A Cambridge University study confirms that practicing conversation for 15 minutes daily is 3 times more effective than studying grammar alone.
8.author: Editorial

s0.title: 1. Information we collect
s0.content: We collect information you provide directly, such as when you create an account (name, email, password), complete your profile (native language, learning languages, biography), or communicate with us.

s1.title: 2. How we use your information
s1.content: We use the information collected to: provide, maintain and improve our services; customize your experience; communicate with you about your account and updates; and assist in keeping the platform safe.

s2.title: 3. Sharing your information
s2.content: We do not sell, trade, or transfer to third parties your personally identifiable information. This does not include trusted third parties who assist us in operating our platform, provided they agree to keep this information confidential.

s3.title: 4. Security
s3.content: We implement security measures to maintain the safety of your personal information. However, no method of transmission over the Internet is 100% secure, so we cannot guarantee absolute security.

s4.title: 5. Cookies
s4.content: We use cookies to enhance your experience. You can choose to have your computer warn you each time a cookie is being sent, or to turn off cookies, but this may affect some site functionality.

s5.title: 6. Your rights
s5.content: You have the right to access, correct or delete your personal information. You can update your data from the profile page or contact us directly.

s6.title: 7. Changes to this policy
s6.content: We may update this privacy policy periodically. We will notify you of any significant changes by posting the new privacy policy on this page.
